To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the EGFR-targeted antibody uptake is inversely related to the EGFR expression level and that the low uptake is due to the low vascular density, poor vascular perfusion, and EGFR binding site barrier in the tumors.
the uptake of anti-EGF antibody in tumors is dependent on tumor vascular density and vascular permeability, not the level of EGFR expression.

the uptake of 64-Cu-DOTA-panimutumab in head and neck squamouse cell carcinoma xenografts with different levels of epidermal growth factor receptors (EGFR) expression was inversely correlated to the expression level of EGFR, and the uptake in tumors with low EGFR expression was due to the low vessel density and the poor vascular permeability of these tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of PET imaging for the study of the biodistribution of 64Cu-labled panitumumah, which is a therapeutic monoclonal antibody (mAb) targeting EGFR.
the development of new methods for the detection and treatment of cancer.
understanding the in vivo kinetics and distribution of anti-EGF receptor (EGFR)-targeted monoclonal antibodies, such as panitumumabs, for the treatment of head and neck cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the EGFR-targeting mAbs have a limited ability to deliver the payload to the tumor cells in the HNSCC models with a high EGFR expression level, which may explain the lack of an apparent correlation between EGFR expression level and the efficacy of anti-EGFr mAb therapy in the clinic.
the EGFR expression level does not directly correlate with the therapeutic efficacy of cetuimab and panituimab in HNSCC.
the lack of correlation between therapeutic efficacy and EGFR expression is likely due to the tumor microenvironment and the EGFR expression level of the tumor cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EGFR-targeted antibodies can be delivered to the tumor, but the delivery is limited by the low tumor vascular density and the binding site barrier.
the EGFR expression level alone is not a good indicator of the therapeutic efficacy of the mAbs.
the tumor microenvironment, not only EGFR expression level, plays a critical role in the efficacy of EGFR-targeted therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EGFR-targeted mAbs may not be effective in tumors with poor vascularization, regardless of EGFR expression.
anti-EGFR antibody therapy is not a good choice for HNSCC patients with high EGFR expression.
EGFR expression alone does not predict the efficacy of anti-EGF mAbs in vivo.
